scope: Theorem 4.1 (Compatible translates from independent pools) of the manuscript “A counterexample to Ryser's covering conjecture” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Rysers-Covering-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 162 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ba76ca1f7af545c6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every positive integer D there is a positive integer K = K(D) with the following property. Let q tend to infinity through prime powers. For each q, let n ≤ Dq, and for 1 ≤ i ≤ n let Wi ⊆ F2 q and let Di be a set of directions, with |Wi| ≤ D, |Di| ≤ D. Assume that each direction belongs to Di for at most D indices i. For distinct indices i, j, declare the translates b + Wi and b′ + Wj to conflict if there are u ∈ Wi, v ∈ Wj, and d ∈ Di ∪ Dj such that (b + u) − (b′ + v) ∈ d. For each i, draw K independent uniform shifts bi,1, . . . , bi,K ∈ F2 q, independently for all indices. With probability tending to one, one can choose ki ∈ {1, . . . , K} for every i so that the translates bi,ki + Wi have no conflicts. The convergence is uniform over all data satisfying the stated bounds.
